_schema.purpose: Allowlist of git hooks you deployed intentionally. A repo-hook auditor reads this to suppress self-detection on hooks you authored. A (path, sha256) match = skip silently. A path match with a DIFFERENT hash = elevated severity, because a known hook was tampered with.

entry_shape.path: absolute filesystem path to the hook
entry_shape.sha256: hex digest of the file contents at time of allowlisting
entry_shape.reason: 1-2 sentences. why this hook exists, what it does
entry_shape.related_decision: path to a memory/Decisions.md or memory/Infra/ entry (optional)

audit_behavior: Path in allowlist AND sha256 matches: skip, log info-level 'allowlisted hook present'.
Path in allowlist BUT sha256 differs: flag ELEVATED 'allowlisted hook tampered', investigate.
Path NOT in allowlist: flag NORMAL severity (a hook you did not record).
lifecycle: Deploying a new legitimate hook: compute sha256, append an entry here, then ship the hook.
Intentionally updating an allowlisted hook: re-compute sha256 and update the entry, or the audit flags drift on the next run.
Removing a hook: remove its allowlist entry to keep the registry tidy.
